newsitem.title: MALI: Mali ruling party wins landslide in troubled poll.
newsitem.headline: Mali ruling party wins landslide in troubled poll.

text.p: President Alpha Oumar Konare's ruling party has won a landslide victory in Mali's rerun parliamentary election but the boycotted poll was a far cry from the nation's widely praised 1992 democratic transition.

Partial results, announced by the election commission late on Tuesday, showed Konare's Alliance for Democracy in Mali (ADEMA) had won at least 93 of the 147 national assembly seats outright in Sunday's first round poll. It had 76 in the old parliament.
ADEMA or its allies won a further 22 seats in the first round either where they put up joint lists or where allied parties contested and won seats in their own right.

With an 18-party radical opposition alliance boycotting the poll, turnout in parts of the capital ranged from 7.4 percent to only 18 percent. The alliance has proclaimed the election a failure and called peaceful marches to force Konare to quit.
It says two people killed in clashes in the town of San on Sunday were its militants and accuses Konare, a historian first elected in 1992, of resorting to violence to hang on to power.
The constitutional court, citing irregularities, scrapped a chaotic April 13 parliamentary election which kicked off the former French colony's second multi-party national elections.
The opposition wanted the election timetable revised. Konare pressed ahead with minor modifications. He won a new five-year term on May 11. The main opposition also boycotted that poll.
April 13 turnout was 30 percent. On May 11, it was just 28 percent. A planned August 3 runoff will now be a formality.
